input.project_brief: CRUD todo app with REST API and a PostgreSQL backend

output.justification: The project is a REST API–fronted CRUD application with no concurrency, distributed coordination, or safety-critical properties. OpenAPI is the canonical choice because it directly models the full API surface — the five standard CRUD endpoints (collection and resource-level GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), path and query parameters, HTTP status codes, and inline JSON Schema definitions for the Todo resource (e.g. id, title, completed, created_at fields). It subsumes plain JSON Schema for payload validation while adding endpoint-level semantics that JSON Schema lacks. No other candidate language (TLA+, CML, Alloy, Event-B) addresses concerns present in this project; their overhead is unjustified for a non-distributed, non-safety-critical system with a trivially simple data model backed by PostgreSQL.
reasoning_steps: Step 1: Identify primary technical concerns — the project is a CRUD todo app with a REST API and PostgreSQL backend. Key concerns are: (1) API surface definition (endpoints, HTTP methods, request/response shapes), (2) data shape validation (todo item schema, field types, constraints), (3) no concurrency or distributed system concerns, (4) no safety-critical requirements, (5) no complex relational invariants beyond standard CRUD.

Step 2: Evaluate candidate languages per concern — API surface: OpenAPI directly models multi-endpoint REST contracts with request/response schemas, HTTP methods, status codes, and path parameters; JSON Schema handles data shapes but lacks endpoint-level semantics. Data shape: JSON Schema and OpenAPI both cover this; OpenAPI subsumes JSON Schema for payload definitions. Concurrency/safety: TLA+, Event-B, CML are all overkill — no distributed coordination or safety-critical properties present. Relational invariants: Alloy could model entity relationships, but the data model is trivially simple (todo items with fields like id, title, status).

Step 3: Weigh candidates — OpenAPI dominates for this project: it covers the full REST API surface (CRUD endpoints: GET /todos, POST /todos, GET /todos/{id}, PUT /todos/{id}, DELETE /todos/{id}), inline schema definitions for the Todo resource, query parameter specs, and HTTP response codes — all in a single artefact. JSON Schema alone would miss endpoint semantics. All other languages (TLA+, CML, Alloy, Event-B, Pydantic) address concerns not present in this project or require a Python-specific context not indicated.
Step 4: Select language and layer — OpenAPI targets the 'api' layer, which is precisely what a REST API contract with request/response definitions represents.
Step 5: Confidence is high (0.95) — the project brief is unambiguous about being a REST API with simple CRUD semantics; OpenAPI is the canonical and most complete fit with minimal overhead.
